questions.prompt: A supported Azure VM workload needs several scheduled recovery points per day, as frequently as every four hours. Which VM backup policy subtype supports this?

options.explanation: It supports the documented multiple-daily VM schedule.

options.text: Only changing Standard daily retention to four years.
options.explanation: Retention length does not create a four-hour schedule.

options.text: Only a storage account tag named Hourly.
options.explanation: Tags do not define VM backup schedules.

options.text: Only a vault NSG allow rule.
options.explanation: Network permission does not define backup frequency.

questions.prompt: Which configuration governs how long backup recovery points remain available?

options.explanation: Start time determines schedule rather than retention duration.
Retention governs how long selected points remain.
DNS caching is unrelated to backup retention.
Notification labeling does not preserve recovery points.

questions.prompt: A backup policy is assigned with the intended schedule, but recent jobs failed. Can you claim the latest scheduled recovery point exists?

options.text: Yes; policy assignment guarantees every recovery point.
options.explanation: Configured intent does not establish job success.

options.text: Yes; any notification email creates the recovery point.
options.explanation: Notifications do not perform the backup themselves.

options.text: No; inspect successful jobs and actual recovery points.
options.explanation: Failed scheduled jobs may not supply the intended point.

options.text: Yes; extending retention recreates missed historical backups.
options.explanation: Retention cannot reconstruct a backup that was not taken.
